image: Studio product photograph of the original 1984 compact all-in-one Macintosh computer: the upright warm-beige plastic case, a small 9-inch black-and-white CRT screen glowing softly with a fine dithered grey pixel pattern and a small blinking text cursor, the 3.5-inch floppy disk slot below the screen, the subtle vents and the recessed handle on top. Three-quarter view from the front-left, slightly low angle so it feels monumental. No keyboard, no mouse, no cables, no logos or lettering on the case. The computer sits right of centre and fills about two thirds of the frame height, leaving calm empty space on the left. Crisp soft-box lighting from the upper left, gentle highlights on the plastic edges, true-to-life colour, ultra detailed, modern museum catalogue aesthetic. Perfectly flat pure black backdrop (#000000) filling every edge of the frame — no floor, no reflection, no gradient, nothing else in the scene.
video: Locked-off studio shot. The computer sits on an unseen, very slow turntable: it turns gently about twenty degrees to show more of its side, pauses, then turns smoothly back to exactly the original angle. The small screen glows and softly flickers like an old CRT, with a faint rolling scanline shimmer. Slow, smooth, calm, premium product-film motion. The flat pure black backdrop stays perfectly black. No new objects, no text, no cuts.
